test: signed edges scored within perturbation, and reversed under over-expression
log: LOOP 243 -- THE SIGN, SCORED WHERE IT MAKES A CLAIM
Loop 242's Q3 compared signed against unsigned over all 8,175 genes and got +0.0001.
The signed graph speaks about a MEDIAN OF 3 of those genes -- 0.037% of the profile,
carrying 0.146% of the response's energy. That gate could not have detected what it
was built to detect. Restricting the correlation instead makes the unsigned arm
degenerate (one value for every target, zero variance), so the instrument changes to
a two-group contrast WITHIN each perturbation, where every perturbation-level
confound cancels exactly.

the gate is JOINT against the BEST SINGLE arm, not against K562 alone. Every A549

R6 FAIL -- combining adds -0.2549 over OTHER ARMS alone, against a 0.02 bar
R7 WHAT THIS CANNOT SHOW
Seven usable factors is few. R5's power comes from the target genes inside them,
not from the count of factors, so one unusual factor can move it -- which is why
the per-factor numbers are printed above rather than only the pooled one.
Over-expression is not the inverse of knockdown. A factor pushed far above its
normal level can occupy sites it never normally occupies, so a failed reversal has
a biological reading as well as a graph-quality one.
The A549 arms sit in a dexamethasone timecourse shared with their control and
matched timepoint by timepoint, so it divides out of the contrast -- but it is not
absent from the biology.
OmniPath signs are a consensus across sources and cell types.
